english.title: Officer / liquidator / property receiver / manager permit invoice etc not to contain statement of winding up
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), being

(A)_[an officer]_
(B)_[a liquidator]_
(C)_[a receiver of property]_
(D)_[a manager of property]_

of a company, namely **(..SPECIFY COMPANY..), which was being wound up, knowingly and wilfully authorised or permitted the default of that company in that

(E)_[not every invoice, order for goods or services, business letter, order form issued]_
(F)_[not all of its websites]_

contained a statement that it was being wound up
english.legislation: Contrary to section 188(2) of, and Schedule 10 to, the Insolvency Act 1986.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
being an officer/liquidator/property receiver/manager
of a company which was being wound up,
knowingly and wilfully permitted the default of that company
in that not every invoice / order for goods / business letter / order form issued / website
contained a statement that it was being wound up.

investigatoraction.description: Guilty Plea by letter procedure may be offered for this offence
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes: Section431 of the Insolvency Act 1986 provides that notwithstanding anything insection 127(1) of the Magistrates' Courts Act 1980, an information relating tosuch an offence which is triable by a magistrates' court in England and Walesmay be so tried if it is laid at any time within 3 years after the commissionof the offence and within 12 months after the date on which evidence sufficientin the opinion of the Director of Public Prosecutions or the Secretary of State(as the case may be) to justify the proceedings comes to his knowledge. Summaryproceedings in Scotland for such an offence shall not be commenced after theexpiration of 3 years from the commission of the offence.
